name: Gradients and Backgrounds Rulebook
summary: When a gradient or background pattern has a job, and how to make one that looks intentional.
check: Measure text contrast at the lightest and darkest point behind it.
View large gradients on an 8-bit screen or a compressed screenshot for banding.

rules.title: A gradient needs a job
rules.text: Lighting a product, setting a time of day, carrying a brand colour across a whole surface, separating a section from the next. "The section looked empty" is not a job (`SL-02`).

rules.title: One signature gradient per site
rules.text: Reuse it in two or three places (hero, one feature, the footer or OG image). Different gradients in every section are noise.

rules.title: Gradients in text or as border glows
rules.text: No gradient-filled headlines (`SL-28`), no glowing gradient borders around cards (`SL-54`).

rules.title: Colours from the palette
rules.text: Stops come from the colour tokens (`CL-04`), or from the hero photo. Never the purple-to-blue default (`SL-01`).

rules.title: Interpolate in OKLCH
rules.text: `linear-gradient(in oklch, …)` avoids the grey, muddy middle that sRGB gradients get between distant hues. Close hues are safer than opposite ones.

rules.title: Few stops, soft transitions
rules.text: Two to four stops. Use easing stops (extra stops along a curve) so there is no visible band edge.

rules.title: Mesh gradients from layered radials
rules.text: Build soft "mesh" backgrounds from two to four overlapping `radial-gradient()` layers on a base colour, or export one from a gradient tool as an image. Keep the brightest area behind the content that matters, not dead centre by reflex (`SL-55`).

rules.title: Fight banding
rules.text: Large smooth gradients band on 8-bit screens. Add very subtle noise (an exported noise PNG at 2–4 % opacity, or noise baked into an exported image), or export with dithering. Grain as a visible effect is a style choice (`SL-08`, `DITHER GRAIN`).

rules.title: Check text on gradients
rules.text: Measure contrast at the lightest and darkest point behind the text, not the average. If it fails anywhere, add a scrim or move the text.

rules.title: Both themes
rules.text: A gradient designed on light may glow on dark. Define a dark variant with lower lightness and chroma.

rules.title: Backgrounds hold back
rules.text: A background texture or pattern sits at low contrast so it never competes with type. If you notice it before the headline, it is too strong.

rules.title: Patterns from a real system
rules.text: Use generated patterns with a clear logic (grid, radial, flow, isometric) from a pattern tool, tuned to the palette, instead of hand-drawn random shapes (`SL-70`).

rules.title: Export the right format
rules.text: SVG for patterns and shapes (optimised with SVGO), AVIF/WebP for photo-like gradients and mesh exports, CSS only when the gradient is simple. Animated shader gradients render only while visible and stop for reduced motion (`PF-21`).

rules.title: Dividers with intent
rules.text: Wave or angled section dividers only when the style is organic or playful, and the same divider shape across the site.

rules.title: Gradients on every button
rules.text: Buttons are solid colours from the palette. A gradient button is a template tell and loses contrast at one end.

rules.title: Animated gradients behind text
rules.text: Text never sits on a background that moves. Animate gradients only where nothing has to be read.
